chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man married a woman on the condition of a servant. He said: 'She gets the middle [portion] of the servants.' I said: 'On a house?' He said: 'The middle [portion] of the houses.'
ai.seo_question: What is the dowry or share of a woman married as a servant according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial rights of a woman when her marriage is contracted with the specific condition of her serving as a domestic servant or concubine. The ruling establishes that she is entitled to a 'middle' or equitable portion of the master's household assets, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle of proportional compensation based on the value of the service rendered. This highlights the contractual nature of such marriages in early Islamic society, where the dowry or compensation was directly linked to her status and duties within the household.
